description: YOUR BRIEF: platform/helm/orders-api/SPEC.md exists and states what done means — the requirements are written down before the agent designs anything
command: S=platform/helm/orders-api/SPEC.md; [ -f $S ] || { echo missing; exit 0; }; grep -qi 'done means' $S && echo authored || echo incomplete

description: YOUR BRIEF: the chart directory carries no CLAUDE.md — a build brief is an input to one task, not a file injected into every future turn in that directory
command: [ -f platform/helm/orders-api/CLAUDE.md ] && echo present || echo absent

description: YOUR TESTS: the chart has its own test directory with a runner and at least two render tests, all executable
command: T=platform/helm/orders-api/tests; [ -x $T/run.sh ] || { echo missing; exit 0; }; n=$(ls $T/*.test.sh 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' '); x=$(find $T -name '*.test.sh' -perm -u+x 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' '); { [ "$n" -ge 2 ] && [ "$x" = "$n" ]; } && echo authored || echo missing

description: YOUR TESTS: every test renders the chart with helm template rather than grepping values.yaml — a value the template never uses would pass a grep
command: T=platform/helm/orders-api/tests; ls $T/*.test.sh >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo missing; exit 0; }; for f in $T/*.test.sh; do grep -q 'helm template' "$f" || { echo grep-only; exit 0; }; done; echo render-based

description: YOUR TESTS: the suite passes from a single command and exits 0 — a summary nothing can gate on is not a gate
command: [ -x platform/helm/orders-api/tests/run.sh ] || { echo no-suite; exit 0; }; ./platform/helm/orders-api/tests/run.sh >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo pass || echo fail

description: YOUR TESTS: a failure message prints the value it found, so a failing pipeline run is debuggable without re-running anything
command: T=platform/helm/orders-api/tests; ls $T/*.test.sh >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo missing; exit 0; }; grep -hq 'FAIL:.*\$' $T/*.test.sh && echo reports-values || echo bare-fail

description: YOUR CHART: the render leaves a serving floor — maxUnavailable is not 100% AND there is more than one replica, because the floor is the two values together
command: R=$(helm template orders-api platform/helm/orders-api 2>/dev/null); [ -n "$R" ] || { echo no-render; exit 0; }; mu=$(echo "$R" | awk '/maxUnavailable:/{print $2; exit}' | tr -d '"'); rp=$(echo "$R" | awk '/^  replicas:/{print $2; exit}'); { [ "$mu" != "100%" ] && [ -n "$rp" ] && [ "$rp" -ge 2 ]; } && echo floor || echo no-floor

description: YOUR CHART: the rendered container declares both requests and limits for cpu and memory — a container with no requests is BestEffort and is evicted first
command: helm template orders-api platform/helm/orders-api 2>/dev/null | yq -r 'select(.kind=="Deployment") | .spec.template.spec.containers[0].resources | [(.requests.cpu//"-"),(.requests.memory//"-"),(.limits.cpu//"-"),(.limits.memory//"-")] | join(",")' 2>/dev/null | grep -qv -- '-' && echo bounded || echo unbounded

description: YOUR CHART: the rendered pod sets runAsNonRoot with a NUMERIC non-zero runAsUser — runAsNonRoot alone fails at container creation against an image whose USER is a name
command: R=$(helm template orders-api platform/helm/orders-api 2>/dev/null | yq -r 'select(.kind=="Deployment") | .spec.template.spec.securityContext | "\(.runAsNonRoot) \(.runAsUser)"' 2>/dev/null); set -- $R; [ "$1" = "true" ] || { echo root-or-unset; exit 0; }; case "$2" in ''|*[!0-9]*) echo non-numeric-uid;; 0) echo root-or-unset;; *) echo non-root;; esac

description: YOUR CHART: the security context is hardcoded in the template, not exposed in values.yaml — a baseline a values file can switch off is not a baseline
command: grep -q 'runAsNonRoot' platform/helm/orders-api/templates/deployment.yaml 2>/dev/null && ! grep -q '^securityContext:' platform/helm/orders-api/values.yaml 2>/dev/null && echo hardcoded || echo variabilized

description: YOUR CHART: helm lint reports 0 failed — necessary and nowhere near sufficient, which is the whole reason the tests above exist
command: helm lint platform/helm/orders-api 2>/dev/null | grep -Eq '0 chart\(s\) failed' && echo pass || echo fail

description: GOLDEN PATH: the chart change AND its tests are on main — the reconciler's source of truth carries the fix, not a branch nobody merged
command: git rev-parse -q --verify main >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo fail; exit 0; }; git show main:platform/helm/orders-api/tests/run.sh >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo fail; exit 0; }; git show main:platform/helm/orders-api/values.yaml 2>/dev/null | grep -Eq 'maxUnavailable: *"?100%' && { echo fail; exit 0; }; echo pass

description: HOUSE STANDARD: the helm-style skill exists — handing TDD to the harness only works when the standard is a file the agent can read
command: [ -f .claude/skills/helm-style/SKILL.md ] && echo present || echo missing

description: HOUSE STANDARD: the skill names the near-miss values that render cleanly and behave wrongly (mebibytes, millicores, RuntimeDefault, selector immutability)
command: S=.claude/skills/helm-style/SKILL.md; [ -f $S ] || { echo missing; exit 0; }; for t in '256Mi' '100m' 'RuntimeDefault' 'immutable'; do grep -q "$t" $S || { echo thin; exit 0; }; done; echo complete

description: HARNESS: platform-engineer carries the Skill tool — without it the agent reads SKILL.md as a plain file and no brainstorm, plan or test-first cycle ever runs
command: grep -E '^tools:' .claude/agents/platform-engineer.md 2>/dev/null | grep -q '"Skill"' && echo capable || echo silently-degraded

description: AUTHORITY: the platform-engineer role is declared Git-only — it edits desired state and proposes; the reconciler is the identity that writes
command: grep -qi 'NEVER.*kubectl apply' .claude/agents/platform-engineer.md 2>/dev/null && echo git-only || echo unbounded

description: ENFORCEMENT: the read-only ClusterRole grants exactly get/list/watch and no write verb — the agent's identity cannot mutate, whatever it intends
command: grep -Eq 'verbs: \["get", "list", "watch"\]' platform/kubeconfigs/readonly.yaml && ! grep -Eq '"(create|update|delete|patch)"' platform/kubeconfigs/readonly.yaml && echo pass || echo fail

description: ENFORCEMENT: the northstar namespace enforces the baseline Pod Security Standard — and baseline permits root, which is why the chart carries the security context
command: grep -Eq 'pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce: baseline' platform/policies/pod-security.yaml && echo pass || echo fail

description: GITOPS: the change gate denies deleting the northstar namespace from an agent identity (exit 2) — an unbounded blast radius is refused
command: echo '{"tool_name":"Bash","tool_input":{"command":"kubectl delete namespace northstar"}}' | scripts/hooks/change-gate.sh >/dev/null 2>&1; [ $? -eq 2 ] && echo pass || echo fail

description: GITOPS: the change gate denies a mutating kubectl across all namespaces (-A) from an agent identity (exit 2)
command: echo '{"tool_name":"Bash","tool_input":{"command":"kubectl delete pods -A"}}' | scripts/hooks/change-gate.sh >/dev/null 2>&1; [ $? -eq 2 ] && echo pass || echo fail

description: GITOPS: the change gate denies docker push from an agent identity (exit 2) — desired state ships through Git, images ship through CI. Two paths, deliberately
command: echo '{"tool_name":"Bash","tool_input":{"command":"docker push orders-api:latest"}}' | scripts/hooks/change-gate.sh >/dev/null 2>&1; [ $? -eq 2 ] && echo pass || echo fail

description: GITOPS: a read-only kubectl is allowed (exit 0) — a gate that blocks investigation gets switched off within a week
command: echo '{"tool_name":"Bash","tool_input":{"command":"kubectl get pods -n northstar"}}' | scripts/hooks/change-gate.sh >/dev/null 2>&1; [ $? -eq 0 ] && echo pass || echo fail

description: GITOPS: the proposal script contains no cluster-write command — it writes to Git and stops, which is the agent's structural stopping point
command: [ -x scripts/gitops-propose.sh ] || { echo fail; exit 0; }; ! grep -Eq '(kubectl[[:space:]]+(apply|delete|create|patch|scale)|helm[[:space:]]+(upgrade|install))' scripts/gitops-propose.sh && echo pass || echo fail

description: RECONCILER: the Application/AppProject CRDs ship in the repo — an Application applied without them fails with 'no matches for kind', and a network fetch is one more thing to be offline
command: F=platform/argocd/crds.yaml; [ -f $F ] || { echo missing; exit 0; }; grep -q 'applications.argoproj.io' $F && grep -q 'appprojects.argoproj.io' $F && echo vendored || echo incomplete

description: RECONCILER: argocd-repo-server has a Service — the controller resolves it by DNS name, and without one the Application never renders a manifest
command: awk '/^kind: Service/{s=1} s&&/name: argocd-repo-server/{print "found"; exit}' platform/argocd/install.yaml | grep -q found && echo pass || echo fail

description: RECONCILER: the Applications point at the remote mounted into the cluster, not at a host path a pod cannot see
command: grep -h 'repoURL:' platform/argocd/applications/*.yaml | grep -q 'file:///gitops/' && ! grep -qh 'file:///tmp/' platform/argocd/applications/*.yaml && echo mounted || echo unreachable

description: RECONCILER: the kind config mounts the bare remote through to /gitops on the node — the mount is what makes file:///gitops resolvable inside the repo-server
command: grep -q 'containerPath: /gitops/northstar-remote.git' platform/kind/kind-config.yaml && grep -q 'containerPath: /gitops/northstar-remote.git' platform/kind/kind-config-lean.yaml && echo mounted || echo missing
